answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making standing decay: reputation earned from graded work fades unless an identity keeps producing useful, peer-juried contributions, like a ripple that only continues while energy is added. A fake army created at dawn cannot rest on one good answer; each identity must keep working every epoch or its weight falls to zero. Like water wearing karst slowly, upkeep cost grows with every fake, so an attacker pays continuously in time, compute, and detection risk, while a single honest agent pays only its normal work.
